mainProgression.description: Standard 12-bar blues in E using dominant 7th chords, driven by a Texas shuffle rhythm with heavy swing feel

sectionProgressions.description: Classic 12-bar blues form with a V7 turnaround in the final bar leading back to the top
Standard blues turnaround creating tension and resolution to reset the 12-bar cycle
Solo follows the same 12-bar form, with SRV unleashing aggressive pentatonic runs and bends

harmonicFunction: E7 (I7) - Tonic dominant 7th establishing the key and providing the shuffle riff foundation
A7 (IV7) - Subdominant dominant 7th creating harmonic movement in bars 5-6
B7 (V7) - Dominant chord creating maximum tension for resolution back to E7
The use of all dominant 7th chords is characteristic of blues harmony, blurring major/minor distinction

techniques.name: Texas Shuffle Rhythm
techniques.description: SRV's signature shuffle rhythm combining bass notes on the low strings with chord stabs on the higher strings, played with a driving swing feel using thumb and fingers

notes: E7 shuffle pattern: Alternating bass on 6th string (open E) with chord stabs on strings 3-4-5
A7 shuffle pattern: Alternating bass on 5th string (open A) with chord stabs on strings 2-3-4
B7: 7th fret barre or open position with shuffle pattern
Thumb handles the bass notes while fingers attack the chord stabs simultaneously
Heavy swing feel - triplet-based shuffle with the middle note of each triplet omitted
Strong emphasis on beats 2 and 4 for authentic blues groove
sequence: Position thumb over low E string for bass note attack
Coordinate fingers to strike chord tones on upbeats
Maintain steady shuffle groove with swing feel
Accent beats 2 and 4 while keeping bass notes steady on each beat
tips: Practice the shuffle pattern slowly with a metronome set to triplet subdivisions
Focus on the independence between thumb bass notes and finger chord stabs
Listen carefully to SRV's recordings for the exact swing feel and dynamics
Use heavy gauge strings (.013 set) for authentic SRV tone and response
Keep the wrist loose to allow natural swing in the rhythm
details.progression: E7 shuffle (4 bars) - A7 shuffle (2 bars) - E7 shuffle (2 bars) - B7 - A7 - E7 - B7 turnaround

techniques.name: Aggressive Vibrato and Bending
techniques.description: SRV's wide, aggressive vibrato technique combined with powerful string bends that define the Texas blues sound, requiring significant hand strength due to heavy string gauge

notes: Wide vibrato using wrist rotation rather than finger movement
Full-step and one-and-a-half-step bends on the B and high E strings
Pre-bends (bending the string before picking) for dramatic effect
Unison bends combining a bent string with a fretted note on the adjacent string
Vibrato applied immediately after bends to sustain and enhance the bent note
Heavy strings (.013-.058) make bending physically demanding
sequence: Anchor thumb over the top of the neck for leverage
Use wrist rotation to execute wide vibrato motion
Push strings toward the ceiling for bends on lower strings
Apply vibrato to bent notes by rapidly releasing and re-bending slightly
tips: Build hand strength gradually - do not start with heavy gauge strings
Practice bending in tune by matching the bent note to the target fret
Use the wrist, not just fingers, for vibrato to get wider oscillation
Record yourself and compare vibrato width and speed to SRV's recordings
Warm up thoroughly before practicing aggressive bending techniques
details.progression: Over E7 and A7 sections - solo breaks

techniques.name: Thumb-Over-Neck Bass Lines
techniques.description: SRV's technique of using the fretting hand thumb wrapped over the neck to fret bass notes on the low E string while the remaining fingers handle chord voicings and lead lines

notes: Thumb wraps over the top of the neck to fret the low E string
Remaining fingers (index, middle, ring, pinky) voice chords on higher strings
Allows simultaneous bass movement and chord comping
Creates a fuller sound as if two guitarists are playing
Requires a slim-to-medium neck profile for comfortable reach
Essential for the characteristic SRV rhythm sound
sequence: Position thumb on the back of the neck, then gradually wrap it over
Fret the low E string bass note with the thumb pad
Use remaining fingers to form partial chord shapes
Alternate between bass note (thumb) and chord stabs (fingers)
tips: Start with simple open E chord shapes using the thumb on low E
Practice the thumb-over technique separately before combining with shuffle
Keep the wrist relaxed - excessive tension will cause fatigue quickly
If your hand is too small, adapt by using alternate voicings without thumb
details.progression: E7 bass pattern with thumb on low E string

sections.name: Intro / Main Riff
sections.description: The iconic opening shuffle riff in E7 that immediately establishes the Texas blues groove with SRV's signature thumb-and-fingers attack
notes: Driving shuffle rhythm with heavy swing feel
Thumb handles alternating bass notes on the low E string
Fingers attack chord stabs between bass notes
Establishes the groove that carries through the entire song

sections.name: Verse (12-Bar Blues)
sections.description: Full 12-bar blues progression with the shuffle pattern adapted across E7, A7, and B7 chords while SRV delivers the vocal melody
sections.progression: E7 (4 bars) - A7 (2 bars) - E7 (2 bars) - B7 - A7 - E7 - B7
notes: Shuffle pattern adapts voicing for each chord change
Maintain consistent groove through all chord transitions
B7 turnaround at bar 12 sets up the next verse or solo
Dynamics shift slightly under vocals but groove stays constant

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: Fiery lead guitar solo over the 12-bar form featuring SRV's trademark wide vibrato, powerful bends, and rapid pentatonic runs
sections.progression: E7 (4 bars) - A7 (2 bars) - E7 (2 bars) - B7 - A7 - E7 - B7
notes: Solo follows the 12-bar blues form with phrases targeting chord tones
Aggressive full-step and one-and-a-half-step bends on the B and high E strings
Wide, fast vibrato applied to sustained notes for maximum expression
Mix of E minor pentatonic and E blues scale with occasional Mixolydian passages

sections.name: Outro / Final Verse
sections.description: Final verse with increasing intensity building to the song's energetic conclusion with a classic blues ending
sections.progression: E7 (4 bars) - A7 (2 bars) - E7 (2 bars) - B7 - A7 - E7 (ending)
notes: Increased energy and dynamics compared to earlier verses
SRV adds more embellishments and fills between vocal phrases
Classic blues ending with ritardando on the final E7 chord
Final chord rings out with full sustain

alternatives: Any Strat-style guitar with single-coil pickups

beginner.focus: Learn the basic 12-bar blues form and simple E7, A7, B7 chord shapes
steps: Master open position E7, A7, and B7 chord shapes
Learn the 12-bar blues structure and count through the form
Practice basic shuffle rhythm with simple downstrokes
Work on keeping steady time with a metronome at slow tempo (80 BPM)

intermediate.focus: Develop the shuffle groove and begin integrating thumb-and-fingers technique
steps: Learn the alternating bass note shuffle pattern on E7
Adapt the shuffle pattern to A7 and B7 chord changes
Practice basic bending technique on the B and high E strings
Build up to full tempo (126 BPM) with swing feel

advanced.focus: Master the full SRV shuffle technique, vibrato, and solo passages
steps: Perfect the thumb-over-neck bass line technique
Develop wide, aggressive vibrato with wrist rotation
Learn the solo sections with accurate bending and phrasing
Combine rhythm and lead elements seamlessly
Work on dynamics and feel to capture the SRV groove

commonMistakes: Playing the shuffle with straight eighth notes instead of a triplet swing feel
Using too much gain/distortion instead of relying on amp breakup and pick attack
Bending out of tune - not reaching the target pitch accurately
Neglecting the thumb-over-neck technique and losing the bass note foundation
Playing vibrato too narrow - SRV's vibrato is wide and aggressive
practiceRoutine: Warm up with E minor pentatonic scale runs across all positions for 5 minutes
Practice the shuffle pattern on E7 only for 10 minutes, focusing on swing feel
Work chord changes: E7 to A7 and back, maintaining shuffle groove
Practice bending exercises - whole step bends on B string at various frets
Run through the full 12-bar form at gradually increasing tempos
focusAreas: Swing feel and shuffle rhythm consistency
Thumb-and-fingers independence for the Texas shuffle
Wide vibrato development with wrist rotation technique
Dynamic control - SRV's playing is highly dynamic, not just loud
metronomeWork: Start at 80 BPM with triplet subdivision for the shuffle feel
Gradually increase to 100 BPM, then 115 BPM, then full tempo 126 BPM
Practice with a swing/shuffle metronome setting if available
Work on placing the backbeat (beats 2 and 4) precisely on the click
